description.value: The study examined behavioral and fMRI BOLD responses during cognitive reappraisal of three socio-emotional stimulus types in patients with generalized social anxiety disorder and healthy controls.

design.value: A randomized controlled trial baseline sample was used to compare 27 unmedicated adults with generalized SAD and 27 healthy controls during three socio-emotional fMRI tasks. Each task included React and Reappraise conditions, and analyses examined behavioral ratings, whole-brain BOLD signal magnitude, early and late BOLD responses, common responses, and between-group effects.

name.value: Anxiety Disorders Interview Schedule for DSM-IV-TR Lifetime version (ADIS-IV-L)

description.value: Two PhD-level clinical psychologists assessed each potential participant using the Anxiety Disorders Interview Schedule for DSM-IV-TR Lifetime version.
This questionnaire assesses both fear and behavioral avoidance of social situations.
Handedness was assessed using the Edinburgh Handedness Inventory.
After each trial, participants provided a negative emotion rating using a button response pad by responding to “How negative do you feel?” from 1 = not at all to 5 = very much.

source_definition.value: The contrast of Reappraise versus React conditions.

association_direction.value: greater late DMPFC responses were associated with greater reduction in negative emotion ratings in SAD patients

description.value: 27 (12 women) unmedicated adults who met DSM-IV-TR criteria for primary generalized SAD; the subgroup was selected from 67 eligible patients and had LSAS-SR scores of 85–102.

inclusion_criteria.value: met clinical diagnostic criteria for a principal diagnosis of current generalized SAD
greater than moderate anxiety/fear for five or more distinct social situations

exclusion_criteria.value: current psychiatric disorders other than SAD, generalized anxiety disorder, agoraphobia without a history of panic attacks, dysthymia, or specific phobia

recruitment_method.value: clinician referrals and advertisements on community and online bulletin boards

medical_condition.value: current Axis-I co-morbidity included panic attacks, generalized anxiety disorder, dysthymia, and specific phobia; past Axis-I co-morbidity included major depression, post-traumatic stress disorder, substance abuse, and eating disorder

diagnostic_instrument.value: Anxiety Disorders Interview Schedule for DSM-IV-TR Lifetime version (ADIS-IV-L)

clinical_characteristics.value: The selected subgroup had LSAS-SR scores ranging from 85 to 102; 13 patients reported past non-cognitive-behavioral psychotherapy and seven reported past pharmacotherapy.

medication_status.value: unmedicated, with a minimum of three months since stopping pharmacotherapy; potential patients were excluded if they reported current pharmacotherapy or psychotherapy

education_summary.value: Patients and HC did not differ significantly in years of education.

task_description.value: Participants viewed color photos of faces displaying Ekman facial action coded anger and contempt facial expressions. Each trial consisted of a cue, a looming harsh facial stimulus, and a negative emotion rating.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed either to react normally without attempting to control, modify, or regulate their reactions, or to down regulate negative emotion reactions by actively reinterpreting the meaning of the emotion inducing stimulus.

stimuli.value: Color photos of faces displaying anger and contempt facial expressions, appearing to move closer to the participant to simulate looming.

task_performance_measures.value: negative emotion rating after each trial on a 1–5 scale
percent reduction in negative emotion when reappraising faces

task_description.value: Participants viewed videotaped actors delivering social criticism and social praise with harsh or happy evaluation-congruent facial expressions. Only the 7.5-s evaluation period of the social criticism trials was included in the analysis.

instructions.value: Participants were asked either to just watch or to reframe their reaction. They were told to react to criticism by reflecting on how the statement represents something true about themselves, or to reappraise by thinking, for example, “this is not always true” or “this is only a thought, not a fact”.

stimuli.value: Video clips from five male and five female actors delivering social criticism or praise while displaying harsh or positive facial expressions.

task_performance_measures.value: negative emotion rating after each video clip on a 1–5 scale
percent reduction in negative emotion when reappraising criticism

task_description.value: Participants read autobiographical social anxiety situations containing negative self-beliefs and were asked either to react to the negative self-beliefs or to reframe their reaction.

instructions.value: Participants were trained to react to the negative self-beliefs by reflecting on how the statement represents something true about themselves, or to reappraise by thinking of a positive coping statement that directly challenges the thoughts.

stimuli.value: An experimenter-composed neutral situation and four participant-generated autobiographical social anxiety situations characterized by social anxiety, humiliation, and/or embarrassment, with participant-provided negative self-beliefs.

task_performance_measures.value: negative emotion rating after each negative self-belief on a 1–5 scale
percent reduction in negative emotion when reappraising beliefs

description.value: Three-dimensional high-resolution anatomical scans were acquired using a fast spin-echo spoiled gradient recall sequence.

AFNI preprocessing included analysis of potential outliers, volume registration to a base image, motion correction, 4 mm isotropic Gaussian spatial smoothing, high-pass filtering, linear detrending, and conversion into BOLD signal percentage change in each voxel. The first four images of each functional run were excluded to allow for T2* equilibration effects.

hrf_model.value: Cohen’s gamma variate model of the hemodynamic response function

model_settings.value: Regressors for the React and Reappraise conditions were convolved with the Cohen’s gamma variate model. Baseline parameters removed mean, linear, and quadratic trends and motion-related variance in the BOLD signal. BOLD signal intensity was computed as percentage of signal change.

model_type.value: random-effects model with between-group and one-sample t-tests

model_settings.value: Individual brain maps were converted to Talairach atlas space and second-level group statistical parametric maps were produced according to a random-effects model. Whole-brain between-group t-tests examined the Group by Reappraise versus React effect, and one-sample t-tests separately examined common responses in SAD and HC.

software.value: AlphaSim, a Monte Carlo simulation bootstrapping program in the AFNI library

model_type.value: between-group t-tests of averaged early and late BOLD responses

model_settings.value: Clusters surviving the between-group t-test threshold were masked; percent signal change was extracted for Reappraise and React at the individual subject level; Reappraise minus React was calculated; percent signal change was averaged across the first three time points and the last two or three time points; and between-group t-tests were run separately for early and late responses.

level.value: subject-level regional response followed by between-group analysis
